 2 13.6: probably the olive-wood statue of Athena Polias in the Erechtheum, one

 213.7: Phidias (ca. 4go-ca. 432 B.c.), Athenian sculptor, best known for his
chryselephantine statues of Athena and Zeus.
 213.8: in the History of the Peleponnesian War (431-404 B.c.), Thucydides men-
tions the Athenian fashion of "fastening up their hair in a knot held by a
golden grasshopper as a brooch." The bees, also ascribed to Phidias in early
printings of the poem, may derive from a reference in Walter Pater's Greek
Studies ( 1895) to "the golden honeycomb of Daedalus."
 213.19-20: cf. Isaiah 2.4: "And they shall beat their swords into plowshares,
and their spears into pruninghooks; nation shall not lift up sword against
nation, neither shall they learn war any more."
